blocks.html: We make decisions all the time: if it is raining, take an umbrella; otherwise, leave it at home. An ATM decides too: if the PIN is correct, show the menu; otherwise, show "Wrong PIN".
The programs in Chapter 10 ran every statement from top to bottom, one after another. This is called sequence. Real programs also need:

blocks.html: A condition is an expression that is either true or false , made with relational operators (== , != , > , < , >= , <= ) and logical operators (&& , || , ! ).
Example: a shop gives a free cloth bag when the bill is more than Rs 1000.
If only one statement is controlled, the braces may be left out, but using them always is a good habit.

blocks.html: When there are more than two choices, conditions are checked one by one from the top. The first true condition's block runs, and the rest are skipped. The final else runs if none is true.

blocks.html: Why does 80 not print "Grade B" as well? Because once per >= 75 is true, the ladder stops; later conditions are never checked. This is also why the order of conditions matters: if per >= 33 were checked first, every passing student would get Grade D.

blocks.html: An if inside another if is a nested if. It is used when a second question depends on the answer to the first.
Leap year rule: a year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4 — except century years (divisible by 100), which must also be divisible by 400. So 2024 and 2000 are leap years, but 1900 is not.

blocks.code:
Enter a year: 2024
2024 is a leap year.

Enter a year: 1900
1900 is not a leap year.

Enter a year: 2000
2000 is a leap year.

blocks.html: Did you know? Every "Wrong password", "Insufficient balance" or "Seat not available" message you have ever seen on an app was produced by an if statement just like the ones in this chapter.
Aim: To write and test programs using if, else-if, nested if and switch.

items.html: Type and test. Type Programs 11.1, 11.4 and 11.7. Test each with at least three different inputs, including a wrong input.
Profit or loss. Input cost price and selling price; print "Profit of Rs ___", "Loss of Rs ___" or "No profit, no loss".
Triangle checker. Input three angles. Print whether they can make a triangle (sum is 180 and all are positive). If yes, print whether it is acute, right or obtuse.

ATM PIN. Store a PIN as a constant (e.g. 4321). Ask the user for the PIN; if correct, ask for the amount and print "Please collect your cash" if the amount is a multiple of 100, else "Enter amount in multiples of 100".
Vowel or consonant. Use switch with fall-through to classify a letter (handle both capital and small letters).
Trace by hand. Without running Program 11.6, write the output for 2100 and 2028. Then run it to check.

blocks.html: Record: Write each program, its test inputs and outputs in your practical file.

items.html: Programs use three control structures: sequence, selection and iteration.
if runs a block only when a condition is true; if-else chooses between two blocks.
The else-if ladder checks conditions in order and runs the first true one; order matters.
A nested if puts one decision inside another.
switch compares one int or char value with many constant cases; break stops

blocks.html: fall-through; default handles everything else.

items.html: The ternary operator ?: is a compact if-else that gives a value.
Watch out for = vs == , stray semicolons, missing braces and missing break .
